project_scope.note: Current species anchor is strong morphologically but lacks promoted reusable photo files.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at a leaf axil underwater. In the local Potamogeton anchor, look for alternate two-ranked leaves plus a persistent stipule/prophyll, then confirm the emergent flower spike.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Submerged rhizomatous aquatic with flexible stems; leaves often arranged in two ranks and with conspicuous stipules/prophylls.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Small sessile flowers densely arranged in an emergent spike; local P. illinoensis has four green perianth segments and four stamens.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Small one-seeded drupelet-like units, commonly several per flower.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Leaf width alone is weak. Use the axillary stipule/prophyll, vein pattern and emergent spike together.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Pondweed ID becomes much less vague when you stop staring at leaf width and inspect the leaf axil for the stipule, then follow the stem to the flower spike.

steps.title: 1 · Read the two-ranked leaves
steps.look_for: Broad submerged leaves arranged alternately in two ranks along flexible stems.

steps.title: 2 · Look in the leaf axil
steps.look_for: A conspicuous persistent sheath-like structure at the leaf axil.
steps.why_it_matters: The stipule/prophyll is much more useful than leaf width alone.

steps.title: 3 · Follow the peduncle upward
steps.look_for: A long stalk ending in a dense many-flowered spike above the water.
steps.why_it_matters: Links the submerged vegetative plant to its reproductive identity.

steps.title: 4 · Use a local key for species
steps.look_for: Vein architecture, stipule form and mature fruit together.
steps.why_it_matters: Broad-leaved pondweeds overlap too much for leaf width alone.

comparisons.title: Potamogeton vs generic broad-leaved aquatics
comparisons.rule: Look for the combination of alternate distichous leaves, axillary stipule/prophyll and an emergent dense flower spike.

visual_lesson.caveat: Species-level Potamogeton separation should use a local technical key once reproductive material is available.
